## Getting started

1. From the checkout (the `trirouter` command does not exist yet):

   ```bash
   python install.py --dry-run     # preview every change
   python install.py               # interactive setup
   ```

2. Setup writes the `trirouter` launcher to `~/.trirouter/bin` and puts it on your PATH (Windows: the user PATH;
   macOS / Linux: a link in `~/.local/bin`, with the profile line printed when that folder is not on PATH).
   **Reopen your terminal**, then `trirouter help` and `trirouter doctor`. Tab completion is installed for your shell.

If you move the checkout, run `python install.py` from its new place once. `python install.py <command>` and
`python -m trirouter <command>` always behave like `trirouter <command>`.

## Conventions

* `trirouter <command> [subcommand] [flags]`; flags may come in any order after the command, `--flag=value` and
  `--flag value` are equivalent. An unknown or not-applicable flag is a usage error (exit 2) with a hint.
* `-h` / `--help` anywhere after a command shows its page. Short flags: `-y` --yes, `-n` --dry-run, `-a` --apply;
  boolean ones combine (`-yn`).
* Flags marked "remembered" are saved in `~/.trirouter/config.json` when the command writes.
* Ctrl+C (or Ctrl+D) stops a command at once: exit status 130, child processes ended, files written atomically.
* Exit status: 0 success, 2 usage error, 1 the command ran but failed, 130 interrupted.

## Common tasks

| I want to | Command |
| --- | --- |
| See what setup would do | `trirouter setup --dry-run` |
| Check that everything works | `trirouter doctor` |
| Re-scan skills after adding some to `~/.skills` | `trirouter skills --apply` |
| See, restore or purge quarantined skills | `trirouter quarantine`<br>`trirouter quarantine restore <name>` |
| Change the quarantine retention (0 = never delete) | `trirouter skills --apply --quarantine-days=7` |
| Get the routing decision for a sub-task from a script | `trirouter route --json "add a CSV export"` |
| Check for new or retired models now | `trirouter models --discover` |
| Reach this computer from a phone | `trirouter remote --name "My PC"` |
| Update completion, agents, the skill catalog and docs after a pull | `trirouter sync` |
| Remove everything the installer added | `trirouter uninstall` |

## setup

Detect the AI tools, connect hooks and MCP, link and scan skills.

```
trirouter setup [-y] [-n] [--providers=LIST] [--jev-token-stdin] [--remote[=NAME]] [options]
```

Interactive setup: detect Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity; take an optional JEV / TypeSafe token or OpenRouter key (without one the built-in local classifier decides); connect hooks and the MCP server; install the `trirouter` command and its tab completion; move every tool's skills into ~/.skills, scan them with SkillSpector when it is installed and link them into every tool; generate the worker agents; optionally set up remote access. Every change is shown first, a changed config file keeps a .bak, re-running is safe; `python install.py` with no arguments does the same.

The JEV key is stored protected (Windows DPAPI; owner-only file elsewhere); a plaintext key from an older version is re-saved protected and removed from old backups of config.json.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: every question gets its default answer (skills are moved into the hub, nothing is quarantined or deleted). |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--providers` | `LIST` | every installed, logged-in tool | no | Comma-separated tools to connect: claude, codex, antigravity. |
| `--jev-token-stdin` | - | off | yes (typesafe_api_key or openrouter_api_key) | Read a TypeSafe token or an OpenRouter key (sk-or-...) from the first line of standard input. TYPESAFE_API_KEY / JEV_OPENROUTER_API_KEY win over the saved key. |
| `--jev-token` | `TOKEN` | none | yes (typesafe_api_key or openrouter_api_key) | Deprecated (visible in process listings and shell history): use --jev-token-stdin or the environment. |
| `--openrouter-key` | `KEY` | none | yes (openrouter_api_key) | Deprecated (visible in process listings and shell history): use --jev-token-stdin or the environment. Same as --jev-token=sk-or-... |
| `--remote` | `NAME` (optional) | ask | yes (remote_name) | Also set up remote access, under NAME (default: the saved name or the hostname). |
| `--workdir` | `DIR` | the checkout | yes (remote_workdir) | Folder remote Claude sessions start in. Only used together with remote access. |
| `--no-migrate` | - | off | no | Do not move the skills of other tools into ~/.skills. |
| `--no-completion` | - | off | no | Do not install tab completion into your shell profile. |
| `--allow-skill` | `NAME,...` | none | yes (skillscan.allow) | Never ask about these skills and restore them from quarantine. Names are added to the saved list. |
| `--scan-llm` | `on|off` | off | yes (skillscan.llm) | Add SkillSpector's LLM analysis; skill content then leaves the machine through its provider. |
| `--accept-flagged` | - | off | no (this run only) | Keep every skill rated DO_NOT_INSTALL without asking (like answering "none"); asked again when a skill changes. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |
| `--catalog-only` | `PATTERN,...` | none | yes (skills.catalog_only) | Hub skills whose folder name matches these fnmatch patterns (e.g. gke-*,google-*) stay in ~/.skills and the catalog but are not linked into Claude Code or Codex, so they do not load into every session; the router still names them. Replaces the saved list; `none` clears it. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter setup    # interactive setup (python install.py alone does the same)
trirouter setup --dry-run    # show every change, write nothing
trirouter setup --yes --providers=claude,codex    # unattended, only these two tools
cat key.txt | trirouter setup --jev-token-stdin    # add a TypeSafe token or OpenRouter key from a file and keep the rest
trirouter setup --yes --remote="My PC"    # also set up remote access
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when no logged-in tool was found.

**See also:** [models](#models), [skills](#skills), [remote](#remote), [doctor](#doctor), [uninstall](#uninstall)

## models

Find new models, drop retired ones, test which ones your accounts can use.

```
trirouter models [-n]
trirouter models --discover [-n]
trirouter models --auto=on|off
trirouter models --main=FAMILY|off [--subagent-model=FAMILY|off] [-n]
```

Compares the models each tool offers today (`codex debug models`, `agy models`, the aliases `claude --help` names) with the ones the router knows. A new model is tried with a one-word prompt and becomes selectable when it answers; a Codex or Antigravity model no longer offered leaves the selection. Results go to ~/.trirouter/models.local.json and the worker agents are regenerated. A check that cannot run changes nothing.

Plain `models` also tries every known Codex model (10-60 s each). --discover is the cheap check that also runs by itself once a day in the background (`--auto=off` stops it); `trirouter doctor` shows the last one.

--main and --subagent-model set Claude Code's default session model (~/.claude/settings.json) and the model of subagents that name none (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL). Most prompts are answered in the session itself, so a sonnet session with the router escalating hard work costs far less than an opus session. Both are remembered and re-applied by setup; `off` removes them.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--discover` | - | off | no | Only the daily check: try new models (and ones offered again). |
| `--auto` | `on|off` | on | yes (model_discovery.auto) | Switch the automatic daily check on or off. Given alone, only the setting is saved. |
| `--main` | `FAMILY|off` | unchanged | yes (claude.main_model) | Claude Code's default model for new sessions; off removes it. |
| `--subagent-model` | `FAMILY|off` | unchanged | yes (claude.subagent_model) | The model of Claude subagents that name none (general-purpose, plugin agents); off removes it. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files (models.local.json, worker agents, ~/.claude/settings.json); preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter models --discover    # the daily check now
trirouter models --discover --dry-run    # show what it would add or remove, save nothing
trirouter models    # full check: also try every known Codex model
trirouter models --auto=off    # no automatic daily check
trirouter models --main=sonnet --subagent-model=sonnet    # cheap sessions; the router escalates
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when another model check is already running.

**See also:** [skills](#skills), [doctor](#doctor)

## skills

Scan and re-link skills, regenerate worker agents, rebuild the catalog.

```
trirouter skills [-a] [-y] [--allow-skill=NAME,...] [--scan-llm=on|off] [--accept-flagged] [--quarantine-days=N] [--catalog-only=PATTERN,...]
```

Scans every third-party skill in ~/.skills with SkillSpector (when installed), links the skills into Claude Code and Codex, registers the folder with Antigravity, regenerates the worker agents and rebuilds the skill catalog; expired quarantine entries are purged.

After all scans the skills rated DO_NOT_INSTALL are listed once and you choose which go to quarantine ([a]ll / [n]one / [s]elect, default none); a skill you keep is remembered for its content. With --yes or without a terminal nothing is quarantined, only a warning is printed.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-a`, `--apply` | - | off | no | Write the changes. Without it the command only previews them. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: every question gets its default answer (skills are moved into the hub, nothing is quarantined or deleted). |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--allow-skill` | `NAME,...` | none | yes (skillscan.allow) | Never ask about these skills and restore them from quarantine. Names are added to the saved list. |
| `--scan-llm` | `on|off` | off | yes (skillscan.llm) | Add SkillSpector's LLM analysis; skill content then leaves the machine through its provider. |
| `--accept-flagged` | - | off | no (this run only) | Keep every skill rated DO_NOT_INSTALL without asking (like answering "none"); asked again when a skill changes. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |
| `--catalog-only` | `PATTERN,...` | none | yes (skills.catalog_only) | Hub skills whose folder name matches these fnmatch patterns (e.g. gke-*,google-*) stay in ~/.skills and the catalog but are not linked into Claude Code or Codex, so they do not load into every session; the router still names them. Replaces the saved list; `none` clears it. |

**Changes:** Preview by default; --apply writes.

```bash
trirouter skills    # preview what would be linked, quarantined or purged
trirouter skills --apply    # scan, ask the quarantine question once, link
trirouter skills --apply --accept-flagged    # keep every flagged skill after a review
trirouter skills --apply --allow-skill=docx,xlsx    # trust two skills for good
trirouter skills --apply --scan-llm=on    # add the LLM analysis to the scan
trirouter skills --apply --catalog-only=gke-*,google-*    # keep rarely used skills out of every session
```

**See also:** [quarantine](#quarantine), [setup](#setup), [doctor](#doctor)

## quarantine

List, restore or purge skills the scan moved to quarantine.

```
trirouter quarantine [list]
trirouter quarantine restore NAME... [-n]
trirouter quarantine purge [--all] [-y] [-n] [--quarantine-days=N]
```

A quarantined skill (~/.trirouter/quarantine) is linked nowhere and left out of the catalog; it is deleted for good after the retention period (default 3 days, skillscan.quarantine_days; 0 = never) by `setup`, `skills --apply` and a Claude Code session start. Subcommands: list (default), restore, purge.

**Changes:** Changes nothing by itself; see the subcommands.

```bash
trirouter quarantine    # list the quarantined skills
trirouter quarantine restore docx    # bring a skill back
trirouter quarantine purge    # delete the expired ones now
```

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [quarantine restore](#quarantine-restore), [quarantine purge](#quarantine-purge), [skills](#skills)

### quarantine list

Show quarantined skills and when they will be deleted.

```
trirouter quarantine [list]
```

One line per quarantined skill: name, quarantine date, the date it is purged (and the time left) and the scan's risk score. The purge date uses the current retention setting.

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

```bash
trirouter quarantine    # same as `quarantine list`
```

**See also:** [quarantine restore](#quarantine-restore), [quarantine purge](#quarantine-purge)

### quarantine restore

Move a quarantined skill back into ~/.skills.

```
trirouter quarantine restore NAME... [-n]
```

Moves the newest quarantined copy of each NAME back to ~/.skills/NAME, provided that name is free, and adds it to skillscan.allow like --allow-skill does, so it is not flagged again. It is linked into the tools by the next `trirouter skills --apply`.

Arguments: NAME... one or more quarantined skill names (see `quarantine list`).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter quarantine restore docx    # restore one skill
trirouter quarantine restore docx xlsx -n    # preview restoring two
trirouter skills --apply    # then re-link
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when a name was not found or the hub already has that name.

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [skills](#skills)

### quarantine purge

Delete expired quarantine entries now.

```
trirouter quarantine purge [--all] [-y] [-n] [--quarantine-days=N]
```

Permanently deletes the quarantined skills whose retention has run out (folder and metadata). With --all it deletes every entry, expired or not, after a confirmation. Only entries directly inside ~/.trirouter/quarantine are ever deleted; links are never followed.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | - | off | no | Delete every quarantined skill, not only the expired ones. Asks first. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: every question gets its default answer (skills are moved into the hub, nothing is quarantined or deleted). |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |

**Changes:** Changes files (deletes for good); preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter quarantine purge    # delete the expired entries
trirouter quarantine purge --dry-run    # show which ones
trirouter quarantine purge --all    # delete everything, after a yes
trirouter quarantine purge --quarantine-days=7    # keep entries a week from now on
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when --all was not confirmed (nothing deleted).

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [skills](#skills)

## remote

Set up or remove phone / other-device access.

```
trirouter remote [--name=NAME] [--workdir=DIR] [--start-session=on|off] [-n]
trirouter remote --remove [-n]
```

Starts each tool's own remote service at logon (Claude Code Remote Control, Antigravity, Codex) under one machine name. Only the connection opens; sessions start from the Claude app, claude.ai/code, the ChatGPT app or antigravity.google.com. See docs/remote-access.md.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` | `NAME` | saved name or hostname | yes (remote_name) | The machine name shown on your other devices. |
| `--workdir` | `DIR` | saved folder or the checkout | yes (remote_workdir) | Folder remote Claude sessions start in; it must be a trusted Claude Code folder. |
| `--start-session` | `on|off` | off | yes (remote_start_session) | on: Claude's server also pre-creates one session at every logon; off: only the connection. |
| `--remove` | - | off | no | Remove the remote-access services instead of creating them. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files and system services; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter remote --name "My PC"    # set up under a name
trirouter remote --name "My PC" --workdir ~/code    # choose the working folder
trirouter remote --start-session=on    # also pre-create a Claude session at logon
trirouter remote --remove    # undo
```

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [doctor](#doctor)

## sync

Bring everything generated from the sources up to date (after a pull or a change).

```
trirouter sync [--check]
trirouter sync --pre-commit
```

Run after a pull or a change: refreshes the installed tab-completion scripts (profiles untouched), the worker agents of the tools that have generated ones and the skill catalog, and in a trirouter checkout regenerates docs/cli.md and sets git's core.hooksPath to .githooks (never over your own hooks). The daily background check refreshes the user-side items by itself.

The pre-commit hook runs `trirouter sync --pre-commit`: the sync, `git add docs/cli.md`, a CHANGELOG reminder, the tests and, when routing code is staged, the evaluation. `git commit --no-verify` skips it once.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | - | off | no | Change nothing; exit 1 when something is out of date (for CI). |
| `--pre-commit` | - | off | no | What the git pre-commit hook runs: sync, stage docs/cli.md, tests, evaluation. Only in a trirouter checkout. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --check.

```bash
trirouter sync    # after a pull or a change
trirouter sync --check    # is anything out of date?
trirouter sync --pre-commit    # the checks the git hook runs, by hand
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when --check found something out of date, an item failed, or a --pre-commit check failed.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [skills](#skills), [doctor](#doctor)

## daemon

The local hook daemon: Claude Code hooks without a Python start per prompt.

```
trirouter daemon [status]
trirouter daemon enable|disable [-n]
trirouter daemon start|stop
```

By default every Claude Code hook starts a Python process (0.3-0.5 s on Windows). With the daemon, Claude Code sends its hooks as HTTP requests to a token-protected trirouter server on 127.0.0.1 (config.json daemon.port, default 47621) that keeps the router and the JEV connection loaded: tens of milliseconds per hook. SessionStart stays a command hook and starts the daemon; if the daemon is down, Claude Code goes on without router context. Codex and Antigravity keep command hooks. Subcommands: status (default), enable, disable, start, stop.

**Changes:** Changes nothing by itself; see the subcommands.

```bash
trirouter daemon    # is it enabled and running?
trirouter daemon enable    # switch Claude's hooks to it
trirouter daemon disable    # back to command hooks
```

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable), [doctor](#doctor)

### daemon status

Show whether the hook daemon is enabled and answering.

```
trirouter daemon [status]
```

Prints the hook transport (command or http), whether the daemon answers on its port, its process id, start time and answer time, and whether Claude's settings.json carries the daemon's token.

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

```bash
trirouter daemon status    # the report
```

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable), [daemon start](#daemon-start)

### daemon enable

Send Claude Code's hooks to the daemon over HTTP.

```
trirouter daemon enable [-n]
```

Sets hooks.transport = http in config.json, starts the daemon and rewrites trirouter's Claude Code hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json as http hooks (SessionStart stays a command hook; a .bak of the original is kept). Takes effect in new and running sessions after Claude Code re-reads its settings.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter daemon enable    # switch
trirouter daemon enable -n    # preview
```

**See also:** [daemon disable](#daemon-disable), [daemon status](#daemon-status)

### daemon disable

Back to command hooks; stop the daemon.

```
trirouter daemon disable [-n]
```

Sets hooks.transport = command, rewrites trirouter's Claude Code hooks as command hooks and stops the daemon.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter daemon disable    # switch back
```

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable)

### daemon start

Start the hook daemon now.

```
trirouter daemon start
```

Starts the daemon in the background unless it already runs (the SessionStart hook does this by itself when the transport is http).

**Changes:** Starts a background process.

```bash
trirouter daemon start    # start it
```

**Exit status:** 0 when it answers. 1 when it did not start (see ~/.trirouter/logs/daemon.log).

**See also:** [daemon stop](#daemon-stop), [daemon status](#daemon-status)

### daemon stop

Stop the hook daemon.

```
trirouter daemon stop
```

Stops the running daemon. With the http transport still enabled the next Claude Code session start starts it again; use `daemon disable` to switch it off for good.

**Changes:** Stops a background process.

```bash
trirouter daemon stop    # stop it
```

**Exit status:** 0 when no daemon runs afterwards. 1 otherwise.

**See also:** [daemon start](#daemon-start), [daemon disable](#daemon-disable)

## learn

Train the local routing model on JEV's past decisions.

```
trirouter learn [-n]
```

Trains a small local classifier on JEV's decisions for your own prompts (~/.trirouter/logs/routing.jsonl) plus the repository's labelled prompts, saved to ~/.trirouter/state/distilled.json. It is enabled only when cross-validation shows it routes like JEV; confident prompts then skip the JEV call. Retrained by itself in the daily background check; ROUTER_DISTILLED=0 switches it off.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Writes ~/.trirouter/state/distilled.json; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter learn    # train, measure and save
trirouter learn --dry-run    # only measure
```

**See also:** [route](#route), [doctor](#doctor)

## doctor

Read-only health report.

```
trirouter doctor
```

Checks the tools (installed, version, logged in), hooks, MCP entries, skill hub and agents, configuration, interpreters, the `trirouter` command, the quarantine and recent router activity. Problems are marked [!!] with the command that fixes them.

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

```bash
trirouter doctor    # print the report
```

**Exit status:** 0 always: read the [!!] lines for problems. 2 on a usage error.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [skills](#skills)

## route

The routing decision for one prompt or sub-task.

```
trirouter route [--provider=NAME] [--json] [--] TEXT...
```

Runs the same pipeline as the hooks for one prompt, with no side effects (no queue state, no log). With no TEXT the prompt is read from stdin. Without --json it prints the [router] instruction; with --json one object: provider, model, effort, agent, tier, task, difficulty, extra_agents, destructive, skill, verify, lang, backend, text, note (for Claude, model is always concrete). #norouter / #privat prompts are not routed. `route` must be the first argument; everything after `--` is prompt text.

Arguments: TEXT... the prompt (free-form; quote it or use --).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider` | `NAME` | claude | no | Whose worker names and models to answer with. |
| `--json` | - | off | no | Print one JSON object instead of the instruction text. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

```bash
trirouter route "add a pagination parameter to the quotes API"    # the instruction text
trirouter route --json --provider codex "fix the flaky login test"    # machine-readable
echo "refactor the parser" | trirouter route --json    # prompt from stdin
trirouter route -- --not-an-option    # text that starts with dashes
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown option, empty prompt). 1 on an unexpected error.

**See also:** [doctor](#doctor)

## uninstall

Remove hooks, MCP entries, remote access and the trirouter command.

```
trirouter uninstall [-n]
```

Removes the router's hooks and MCP entries from Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity, the remote-access services, the `trirouter` launcher with its PATH entry and the tab completion in your shell profiles. Your skills stay in ~/.skills (and linked).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

```bash
trirouter uninstall --dry-run    # show what would be removed
trirouter uninstall    # remove it
```

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [remote](#remote)

## help

Show the manual of a command.

```
trirouter help [COMMAND [SUBCOMMAND]]
```

Prints the man-page-like help of a command. `trirouter <command> --help` does the same; docs/cli.md holds every page (regenerated by `trirouter sync`).

Arguments: COMMAND a command name; SUBCOMMAND for quarantine and daemon.

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

```bash
trirouter help    # the command list
trirouter help skills    # the skills page
trirouter help quarantine purge    # a subcommand
```

**See also:** [doctor](#doctor)
